purpose: Move counts while preserving table margins and follow their discrepancies into one statistic.
meaning: The Pearson chi-square statistic adds squared observed-minus-expected discrepancies divided by expected counts. Independence expected counts use row total times column total divided by grand total. This lesson computes a statistic without an unqualified significance claim.

definition.setting: Forty constructed readers are classified by desk (A/B) and preference (paper/digital). The 2×2 table is [[d,20−d],[20−d,d]]. Both row and column totals are fixed at 20, making every expected independence count 10.

signature.d: Two matching diagonal counts in a fixed-margin table.

conditions: Forty constructed readers are classified by desk (A/B) and preference (paper/digital). The 2×2 table is [[d,20−d],[20−d,d]]. Both row and column totals are fixed at 20, making every expected independence count 10.
